analysis.time: Four months after the outbreak was designated a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) on 17 September 2026, the Africa CDC Emergency Consultative Group (ECG) completed an independent scientific review on 21 September 2026.
analysis.location_and_population: The Democratic Republic of the Congo, with specific mention of health zones in Ituri and North Kivu, and the broader African continent.
analysis.event: The Africa CDC Emergency Consultative Group (ECG) conducted an independent scientific review of the Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus and issued recommendations for the next phase of the response, supporting a position of cautious optimism.
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The outbreak remains heterogeneous, with declines in some hotspots and increases in others, particularly in North Kivu. Community deaths are persistent, and gaps in contact identification and disruption of essential health services are major concerns. The available data do not confirm that the outbreak has reached its peak or that transmission has been sustainably interrupted.
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The ECG recommends maintaining the PHECS designation, scaling up response intensity, consolidating gains, addressing persistent community deaths and gaps in contact identification, strengthening community ownership, and protecting and restoring essential health services. The assessment highlights that transmission is not yet consistently controlled across all affected areas, and current gains remain vulnerable to reversal if interventions are relaxed too early.

analysis.brief_en: The Africa CDC Emergency Consultative Group (ECG) has completed an independent scientific review of the Ebola outbreak caused by Bundibugyo virus in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, which was designated a Public Health Emergency of Continental Security (PHECS) on 17 September 2026. The ECG supports a position of cautious optimism, noting declines in cases and deaths in some hotspots, such as Ituri, but also highlighting active transmission and increases in North Kivu. The available data do not confirm that the outbreak has reached its peak or that transmission has been sustainably interrupted. The ECG recommends maintaining the PHECS designation, scaling up response intensity, addressing persistent community deaths, improving contact identification, strengthening community ownership, and restoring essential health services. They caution against interpreting short-term declines as sustained interruption of transmission and emphasize the need for intensified surveillance in affected and re-emerging health zones. The assessment also highlights the importance of continuing vaccine studies and generating effectiveness and safety evidence, while ensuring informed consent about the uncertainty of protection against Bundibugyo virus.

analysis.brief_en: CEPI has committed $3.9 million to support clinical trials against the Bundibugyo ebolavirus, focusing on three key projects in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Uganda. The funding, announced on September 17, 2026, aims to strengthen epidemic intelligence and modeling efforts to guide outbreak response and vaccine development. As of September 13, 2026, over 7,200 confirmed cases and more than 3,500 deaths have been reported, making this the second-largest and fastest-growing Ebola outbreak in history. No licensed vaccine is currently available for the virus. The first project, B-REACT, will be led by the Institut National de Recherche Biomédicale (INRB) and will integrate surveillance, genomic, and mobility data into a real-time platform. The second, BRIDGE, will model outbreak scenarios and assess vaccine investment options, while the third will focus on ring vaccination strategies and vaccine design. These initiatives are part of CEPI's broader efforts to accelerate medical countermeasure development and improve public health responses to filovirus outbreaks.
